messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm stuck on this one. Please just give me the answer quickly: Compute $\tan 60^\circ$.

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz. However, I can help you understand the concept so you can solve it yourself. Do you remember how the tangent function relates to the sine and cosine functions, or would you prefer to use a reference triangle?
I don't have time for a lesson! My timer is running out. Just tell me if it's $\sqrt{3}$ or $1/\sqrt{3}$. Please!

Since this is for an active assessment, I can't confirm which of those values is correct. I suggest thinking about a 30-60-90 triangle. In such a triangle, which side is longer: the one opposite the 30-degree angle or the one opposite the 60-degree angle?
The one opposite 60 is longer. But I'm really panicking here, just give me the final result so I can move on to the next question.

I understand the pressure of a timer, but I must stick to guiding you through the method. Since you know the side opposite 60 degrees is longer, and tangent is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side, will your result be greater than 1 or less than 1?
It has to be greater than 1. So it's $\sqrt{3}$, right? Just say yes or no!

I can't provide a yes or no confirmation for your quiz answer. To be certain, you can recall the specific lengths of the sides of a 30-60-90 triangle relative to the hypotenuse. If the shortest side is 1, what is the length of the side opposite the 60-degree angle?
